To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel end-to-end module network architecture for visual question answering, that is capable of learning to reason about compositional questions, and that outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on a recently proposed dataset.
(1) we introduce a new dataset that is targeted at compositional reasoning, and (2) we introduce a model that can learn to reason by generating networks from data.

(i) N2NMNs learn to reason by predicting instance-specific network architectures, (ii) N2NMN architectures discovered from data outperform architectures proposed by a parser, and (iii) the learned architectures are interpretable, and are often more efficient and accurate than the expert-designed baseline.
In summary, our research is concerned with
learning to reason about visual scenes by learning to compose visual reasoning modules.
the question "how can a machine learn to reason by learning to build a network of networks that solve subproblems?"
developing a system that learns how to solve visual question answering tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our N2NMNs are able to learn interpretable networks from scratch that are specialized to the task of answering questions about images.
N2NMN outperforms state-of-the-art models in CLEVR dataset by 50% relative, while discovering interpretables networks for each question.
N2NMN is able to learn to reason by predicting instance-specific network layout without the aid of parser.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new model for visual question answering, which learns to decompose questions into sub-problems and solve them using a network of smaller modules.
N2NMN is able to learn the modular network structure from the training set and achieve better performance than previous methods.
we are the first to propose a model that can learn to reason in an end-to-end fashion, and that can learn to generate network structures from data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show that a neural network can learn to generate and execute its own network structure.
learning to reason can be cast as a sequence prediction problem, and that end-to-end learning of both network layouts and parameters is a viable approach to compositional question answering.
the ability to learn to reason is not limited to the use of a parser.
